title: Create an InnoDB sample table
summary: InnoDB is a storage engine that supports transactions and foreign keys.
introduction: InnoDB is a storage engine that supports transactions and foreign keys. Your task: Explain why the title column uses NOT NULL.
learningObjectives: Explain why the title column uses NOT NULL.
Explain the example for create an innodb sample table

blocks.text: InnoDB is a storage engine that supports transactions and foreign keys. AUTO_INCREMENT supplies an id when a row omits it.

Use MariaDB 10.11+ with its mariadb client in an empty practice database. These dialect-specific examples do not run in the site's SQLite playground. Keep the sample database separate from real records.

blocks.code: CREATE TABLE cma_maria_books(id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,title VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,pages INT) ENGINE=InnoDB;
blocks.title: Create an InnoDB sample table

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: A primary key identifies a row and prevents duplicate key values. Related records can refer to that key.
`NOT NULL` requires a value to be present. It is a separate rule from numeric range checks.

blocks.text: The practice database now has an empty book table with an automatic id column.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Create this table once in the practice database. Table creation is not ordinary rollback-safe row work.
